The argument correctly notes that any net of a regular tetrahedron consists of four equilateral triangles glued together, which always yields six boundary edges after cutting along a spanning tree of three edges. A parallelogram has only four boundary edges, so it cannot be a tetrahedron net. Consequently no regular tetrahedron can be formed from a parallelogram‑shaped net, and the surface area of the “resulting” tetrahedron is indeed zero.
